title: Area of triangles
goal: I can find the area of a triangle.
teach: A triangle is half of a rectangle (or parallelogram) with the same base and height: area = ½ × base × height. The height is perpendicular (at 90°) to the base. Do not use a slanting side as the height.
tvis: area = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 cm²

ex.q: A triangle has sides 13 cm, 13 cm and base 10 cm, and a height of 12 cm. Find its area.
steps: A = ½ × b × h (use the perpendicular height, not the 13 cm side).

watch: Use the perpendicular height, not the slanting side.

qs.text: Base 8 cm, height 5 cm. Find the area.
qs.steps:
1. Formula: area of a triangle A = ½ × b × h, where b is the base and h is the perpendicular height (at 90° to the base).
2. A = ½ × 8 × 5
3. = 20 cm²

qs.text: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 9 cm. Find its area.
qs.steps:
1. Formula: area of a triangle A = ½ × b × h, where b is the base and h is the perpendicular height (at 90° to the base).
2. In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides are the base and the height.
3. A = ½ × 6 × 9 = 27 cm²

qs.text: Base 12 m, height 7 m. Find the area.
qs.steps:
1. Formula: area of a triangle A = ½ × b × h, where b is the base and h is the perpendicular height (at 90° to the base).
2. A = ½ × 12 × 7
3. = 42 m²
